title: Session handles are opaque, high-entropy, and carry no client-readable claims
asA: operator who does not want their session credential to double as a signed self-describing token
iWant: the handle in my browser to be nothing more than a random opaque string that only the server can interpret
soThat: revocation is a server delete and there is no signed payload for anyone to forge, decode, or replay past its expiry

acceptanceCriteria.description: Issued session handles are base64url of at least 24 bytes of entropy; every issue produces a distinct handle across a batch of one thousand.
acceptanceCriteria.given: one thousand sessions are issued in a batch
acceptanceCriteria.then: every handle is a base64url string decoding to at least 24 bytes, and no two handles in the batch are equal

acceptanceCriteria.description: Handles carry no encoded payload; a handle contains no principal id, no expiry, no scope, and no signed segment separable by dots or other JWT-shaped delimiters.
acceptanceCriteria.then: it contains no dot-separated JWT segments, decodes to random bytes, and reveals no substring matching the principal id, expiry timestamp, or scope value stored in the session record

acceptanceCriteria.description: No authenticated response body or header on any code path emits a JWT-shaped token, a signed bearer, or any credential envelope beyond the opaque session cookie.
acceptanceCriteria.given: any authenticated request-response pair on the surface
acceptanceCriteria.when: response headers and body are scanned for JWT-shaped tokens (three dot-separated base64url segments) or Authorization headers with Bearer prefixes
acceptanceCriteria.then: no such artefact is present outside of a Set-Cookie header carrying the opaque session handle
